pr_body:
- Added a `WriteEvent(int, string, string, string, string, string)` overload to avoid allocating the `params object[]` on every `RequestStart/Stop`
- Added `IsEnabled(EventLevel)` checks to avoid the overhead of computing arguments when only counters are enabled (so when the `EventLevel` is higher than `Informational`)


As a side note, I'm not sure how much you care about the Interlocked cost on some of these paths, but it can be improved (putting it behind an IsEnabled check / going from 3 Interlocked operations for Start/Stop to 2)

Fixes #30159
pr_comments: @MihaZupan  do you mind opening an issue for this?
Opened #30159. Out of curiosity, why is it needed in cases like this? It feels like noise.
It occurs to me that I forgot to fix this when I added that change...
I'm not sure why it's needed either. This LGTM

> As a side note, I'm not sure how much you care about the Interlocked cost on some of these paths, but it can be improved (putting it behind an IsEnabled check / going from 3 Interlocked operations for Start/Stop to 2)

Then the counts would be off.

Here you have `started` and `current` counters. You increment both on Start and decrement `current` on Stop.

In runtime we instead have `started` and `stopped` counters. This way there's 1 increment on Start and 1 increment on Stop.
The `current` is calculated from `-stopped + started` in the counter callback.

Doing so essentially saves us 1 interlocked operation on `Start`.
@MihaZupan Were you able to run any benchmarks that showed a measurable improvement due to this change?

> @MihaZupan Were you able to run any benchmarks that showed a measurable improvement due to this change?

Less `object[]` allocations.
I saw this gets rid of the call to the params overload of WriteEvent. I'm just curious if it made a measurable impact. I already approved because it's a clear improvement. I guess we'll see soon.

This affects a few scenarios:

- EventSource is enabled at `Informational` level:
  - We're saving an `object[]` allocation and the less efficient `WriteEvent` code path on every `RequestStart/Stop`
- EventSource is enabled at a high level (for example only critical, such as when only needing `EventCounter`s):
  - We perform the more specific `IsEnabled(level)` check which saves the preparation of all arguments (and associated allocations) and saves the overhead of calling into `WriteEvent` which will eventually do a delayed `IsEnabled` check
  - This should have a measurable overhead reduction for the "metrics only" scenario (essentially same perf as when the EventSource is disabled)
- EventSource is disabled
  - Should have no real difference. `IsEnabled(level)` checks are slightly more expensive than just `IsEnabled()`, but the new `RequestStart/Stop` implementations should inline better so 🤷‍♂️

If you're looking for exact numbers for these I can run some benchmarks. There should be a noticable but small diff for the "telemetry on" scenario judging from the traces where I saw kestrel calling into the varargs overload.

issue_context.title: KestrelEventSource has perf overheads
issue_context.body:
`KestrelEventSource` calls the `params object[]` overload of `WriteEvent` on every `RequestStart` and `RequestStop`. This can be avoided by adding a custom `WriteEvent` overload.

It's also only checking `IsEnabled()`, which means it's adding the overhead of computing arguments even when the `EventSource` is only enabled at a high `EventLevel` - like when only metrics are enabled. This can be fixed by using more specific `IsEnabled` overloads.

Fix: #30150
